title: TOOLS & TRAVEL
blurb: Getting around, making things and paying for them.

radicals.name: WALK
radicals.origin: A crossroads plus a foot: someone on the move. It wraps the left and bottom of a character like a road, and it is written last.
radicals.watch: Some of the most common words kept the road and lost the journey: 这 (zhè, this), 还 (hái, still), 边 (biān, side).

radicals.name: VEHICLE
radicals.origin: The traditional form 車 is a chariot seen from above: an axle through a body with a wheel at each end. The simplified 车 is a quick sketch of it.
radicals.watch: Carts explain a few surprises: 轻 (qīng, light) was a light, fast chariot and 软 (ruǎn, soft) a cushioned one. 输 also means to lose a game.

radicals.name: METAL
radicals.origin: 金 means gold, and metal in general: nuggets in the earth under a cover. Simplified Chinese writes it in five strokes on the left.
radicals.clue: metals and things made of metal
ex: a metal, and 银行 is a bank
a metal, and 地铁 is the subway
a bronze bell told the time
radicals.watch: 错 (cuò, wrong) once meant to inlay gold in a criss-cross pattern. Criss-crossed became mixed up, and mixed up became wrong.

radicals.name: KNIFE
radicals.origin: 刀 is a blade with a handle. On the right side of a character it stands upright as 刂. Elsewhere it keeps its full shape.
ex: a blade cuts into wood or stone
the full 刀 on the right
a knife 刀 splitting something in two 八
radicals.watch: In 到 (dào, to arrive) the knife is the sound part: dāo, dào. It is one of the few common radicals that stands on the right.

radicals.name: MONEY
radicals.origin: 贝 is a cowrie shell. Three thousand years ago cowries were money in China, so the shell became the sign for wealth and trade.
radicals.watch: Two look-alikes: 页 (head, page), as in 顺 and 题, has a line and a tick on top. 见 (to see) ends in a hook to the right.
